clue.text: Regularly play sport, coming first like clockwork

indicators.note: tells us the sport goes at the front, ahead of the letters picked from play

parts.note: swimming is a sport

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals from play, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Advice to play sport often, putting it first in a routine that runs like clockwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' picks L and Y from 'play'; 'coming first' puts SWIMMING ahead of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for proceeding smoothly without any hitch.

clue.text: Indian cricketer liked a VIP I ejected roughly

indicators.note: done roughly, the remaining letters are jumbled into a new order
the letter I is thrown out of the words liked a VIP

explanation.surface: A cricketer who took a liking to a VIP until the VIP was thrown out roughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ejected' drops one I from LIKEDAVIP, and 'roughly' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Kapil Dev is a famous Indian all-rounder who captained India to the 1983 World Cup win.

clue.text: Spanish golfer's bracing new ball game

indicators.note: the golfer's name holds the N between its letters, as a brace grips something

parts.note: Seve Ballesteros was a Spanish golfer, so his possessive gives Seve's

explanation.surface: A Spanish golfer gearing up for a new ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bracing' puts N inside SEVES (Seve's, the apostrophe dropped).
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens is a seven-a-side form of rugby, a game played with a ball.

clue.text: Finish circulating scores in the poolroom

indicators.note: going round, so the word for finish is turned to read backwards

parts.note: to stop is to finish

explanation.surface: A player wraps up a game while scoring in a pool hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating' turns STOP backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In pool and snooker, a ball sunk into a pocket counts as a score.

clue.text: Stumped, falls over, limiting time to resume

parts.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

indicators.note: the reversed falls enclose the letter for time, setting bounds around it
turned over, so the name of the falls is read backwards

parts.note: Niagara is the famous waterfall on the US-Canada border

explanation.surface: A batsman stumped, falls over, and needs time before carrying on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns NIAGARA into ARAGAIN, and 'limiting' puts T inside it to make ARTAGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to begin once more after a pause, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Article in L'Equipe about a hybrid game

indicators.note: the French article goes around the other letters

parts.note: L'Equipe is a French sports paper, so the article there is the French le
a cross is a hybrid of two breeds or varieties

explanation.surface: A French sports paper runs a piece about a hybrid sport.
explanation.walkthrough: L'Equipe is a French sports daily, which is why the article is the French one.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks.

clue.text: British haul in each caviar supplier

indicators.note: the word for haul goes inside the abbreviation for each

parts.note: to lug is to haul or drag

explanation.surface: A British fishing catch, with each one supplying caviar.
explanation.definitionFit: The beluga sturgeon yields the most prized caviar.

clue.text: Cancel large jump on rink

parts.note: to axe a project is to cancel it
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An instruction to drop a big jump from an ice-skating routine.
explanation.definitionFit: An axel is a figure-skating leap with a forward take-off.

clue.text: With sound, bat screens old vessel after 12

parts.note: sound and hale both mean healthy

indicators.note: the bat hides the letter for old within itself

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sturdy bat shields an old ship that chased the creature at 12.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screens' puts O inside BAT. The clue at 12 is a finback, a kind of whale, so the vessel is one sent after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A whaleboat is a long, light rowing boat once launched to hunt whales.

clue.text: One avoids bye by involving a couple

indicators.note: the numeral one stays out of the word for bye

parts.note: adieu is a French word for goodbye
I is the Roman numeral one
X is the multiplication sign, read as by in three by four

explanation.surface: A cricket side avoids conceding byes thanks to a partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoids' takes I out of ADIEU to leave ADEU.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means for two, describing something shared by a pair.

clue.text: Girls manufactured poles I installed

indicators.note: the letter I is put in place inside the other letters

parts.note: something manufactured has been made
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Someone built poles and set them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'installed' puts I inside MADENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidens is an old-fashioned word for young unmarried women.

clue.text: Rare question in exam: 'What's another name for a finback?'

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for rare, as in coin and stamp catalogues

indicators.note: the abbreviation for question goes inside the word for exam

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: An unusual exam question asking for another name of a whale.
explanation.definitionFit: The finback, or fin whale, is a species of rorqual, the term naming it and its relatives.

clue.text: Asian banker's attempt to quit business

indicators.note: the word for attempt leaves the word for business

parts.note: industry is business or commercial activity
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: An Asian bank employee tries to leave the business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is crosswordese for a river, which has banks; here it is not a bank employee.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a great river of Pakistan and India, and a river has banks.

clue.text: Pole identifies Welsh runner

parts.note: to flag something is to mark it out or identify it
the Taff is the river through Cardiff, and a river runs

explanation.surface: A Polish man identifies a Welsh athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person, and 'runner' like an athlete; runner is a crossword word for river.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagstaff is the tall pole from which a flag is flown.

clue.text: Release mother and children, occupants of lodge

parts.note: to release is to free
ma is an informal word for mother
sons are children

explanation.surface: A family of mother and children is let out of a holiday lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of this fraternal order meet in a hall called a lodge.

clue.text: Affair involving Yankee swimmer's sport

indicators.note: the word for affair takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a fling is a brief love affair
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a fish is a swimmer; the 's means is, joining it to the definition

explanation.surface: A romance with an American who swims as a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly fishing is angling with an artificial fly as lure, a pastime and sport.

clue.text: What kind shooters do on Glorious Twelfth, snitch?

definitions.text: What kind shooters do on Glorious Twelfth
definitions.meaning: the Glorious Twelfth is 12 August, when British grouse shooting begins; generous shooters would hand the shot birds to others
to snitch is to tell or betray a secret

explanation.surface: Wondering whether generous grouse shooters on opening day are really informers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Glorious Twelfth, 12 August, opens the grouse-shooting season in Britain; 'game' here means shot birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to reveal a secret, and literally means handing over shot birds.

clue.text: What summers can do to a stile that's rotting?

indicators.note: wood rotting falls apart, so the letters of to a stile break up and rearrange

explanation.surface: Wondering what warm seasons can do to a decaying wooden stile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summers' reads as seasons but means people who do sums.
explanation.definitionFit: A summer, one who sums, adds things up, which is to make a total.

clue.text: Skater trained in West Indies to practise another sport

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the abbreviation for the West Indies
trained means drilled into new shape, so the letters of skater are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ice skater trains in the Caribbean to take up a new sport.
explanation.definitionFit: To waterski is to be towed on skis across water, a verb for doing that sport.

clue.text: The Caymans managed to expel English sailor

indicators.note: managed means handled or worked, so the remaining letters are reorganised
the letter for English is thrown out of the words The Caymans

explanation.surface: Cayman Islands officials managed to deport an English sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to expel' drops E from THECAYMANS, and 'managed' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A yachtsman is someone who sails a yacht.

clue.text: Sort of kick gutless officer investigating deaths

indicators.note: without its insides, so the middle letter of the official's title is removed

parts.note: a coroner investigates sudden or suspicious deaths

explanation.surface: A cowardly coroner and some sort of kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' removes the middle letter, O, from CORONER.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, a set-piece kick from the corner flag is taken after the ball goes out off a defender.

clue.text: All at once, last pair leave, expressing disapproval

indicators.note: the final two letters go away from the word for expressing disapproval

parts.note: tutting is making the tut sound of disapproval

explanation.surface: Two people walk out at once, clicking their tongues in disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last pair leave' removes NG from TUTTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is a musical direction for the whole ensemble playing together.

clue.text: Dainty milk supplier pens Italian book

indicators.note: encloses, as a pen holds animals, so the word for teat holds the other letters

parts.note: tit is a word for a teat, which supplies milk

explanation.surface: A dairy supplier writes a delicate Italian book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' puts ITB inside TIT, after its first T.
explanation.definitionFit: A titbit is a dainty morsel of food; 'dainty' as a noun means a delicacy.

clue.text: Game people lose these going round the bend

definitions.meaning: a children's game with small glass balls

definitions.text: people lose these going round the bend
definitions.meaning: losing them is an idiom for going mad, which is also going round the bend

explanation.surface: A game whose pieces players lose when they go mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Marbles is a children's game, and to lose your marbles is to lose your sanity.

clue.text: Game guy controls more than one private company

indicators.note: holds in check, so the word for ridicule wraps around the other letters

parts.note: to guy someone is to ridicule or mock them
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers such as privates

explanation.surface: A man who runs several private companies is a fair target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a noun but is a verb, to ridicule; 'more than one private' means other ranks, the army's ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Game means wild birds that are hunted, and this one is the male red grouse.

clue.text: Gulf state picked up ENT problem

indicators.note: heard, so the clue uses the sound of the state's name rather than its spelling

parts.note: Qatar is a state on the Persian Gulf

explanation.surface: A Gulf nation caught an ear, nose and throat complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT means ear, nose and throat medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Catarrh is a build-up of mucus in the nose and throat, treated by ENT doctors.

clue.text: See 22
Finds missing disc deliveries

indicators.note: the word disc is absent from the word for finds

parts.note: discovers means finds
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone locates a lost disc among the deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, each a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket overs are made up of deliveries, so the plural stands for many balls bowled.

clue.text: Problem for poultry farmer who's getting on?

definitions.meaning: a farmer of fowls would be troubled by having none of the birds
describes someone ageing, from the idiom no spring chicken

explanation.surface: An ageing poultry farmer faces a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase means having no birds; idiomatically someone no longer young is no spring chicken.
